leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 files prefer a single-part B046 prize (GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapies) with the same three laureates, Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. What is shared: the scientific case (proglucagon processing, GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action in humans, the active truncated peptide, then randomized outcome evidence in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints), high maturity, and a physiology-centred citation. What differs is only wording: some citations name the 'active form' or 'active peptide forms', one names 'insulinotropic action', and none names a specific product. All six also state that the Mojsov credit and the omission of Knudsen and Habener are unresolved, and Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius say the trio would be the wrong one or incomplete if the committee decides the drug development is the essential achievement.

areas_of_agreement: All six members explicitly prefer B046 as the single-part configuration, and none lists a two-part prize as their preferred configuration.
All six name the same three laureates (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) and describe the mechanism-to-patient arc as mature, independently confirmed for decades and with very large clinical impact.

All six place the weak point in attribution, not in scientific merit or maturity, and all cite the three-person cap as forcing a choice among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, with Habener outside the credited names.

Five of six name CAR-T (B028) as an alternative; optogenetics (B038) is named by El Manira, Linnarsson and Perlmann, cGAS-STING (B029) by Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius, SMN2 antisense (B007) by Sandberg, and the unfolded protein response (B011) by Svenningsson. These alternatives are not preferred configurations and no round-1 file puts any of them in a prize part.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should honour the physiology of the hormone and its active peptide form, or the drug development (long-acting analogues) through which most patient impact arrived; all six currently choose physiology but each flags this as the main judgement call.

Perlmann argues the physiology-centred citation need not mention any product; Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius say a physiology-only prize may look incomplete if the committee considers drug development essential. The files do not show disagreement on the underlying science.

Among alternatives, members differ on which is the strongest second achievement: CAR-T for durable remissions (Linnarsson, Wahren-Herlenius), SMN2 antisense for a clear mechanism-to-therapy link (Sandberg, though El Manira notes the engineering component and smaller population), and cGAS-STING for a new innate-immune axis (Perlmann, though El Manira notes no approved therapy). These are secondary to the shared B046 preference.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that long-term safety and central mechanisms of GLP-1 agonists remain under study, and El Manira that long-term safety of obesity indications is still accumulating; no other member raises this.
attribution_disputes: Priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is described as contested by all six; no member says the supplied text lets them settle it between Mojsov and Habener.
Habener is outside the credited names; whether this omission matters is raised explicitly by El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius.

Knudsen's role in designing liraglutide and semaglutide is acknowledged by all six, but the files differ on whether she should displace Mojsov, and none of the six currently prefers a configuration that includes her. The chair's own round-1 statement places Mojsov in the third slot.

Alternatives carry separate attribution questions: Eshhar is outside the credited names for B028 (El Manira, Linnarsson, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius), Ishikawa's and Vance's roles are open for B029 (El Manira, Svenningsson), and six-way optogenetics credit would need to be reduced to three (Linnarsson).
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B046; all six call it high and independently confirmed.
cGAS-STING (B029) is questioned on maturity by El Manira and Perlmann because STING agonists and inhibitors have not yet produced approved therapies.
Optogenetics (B038) is described by El Manira as a tool with only beginning clinical use, as opposed to a disease mechanism.
Long-term safety evidence for obesity indications of GLP-1 agonists is still accumulating (El Manira, Wahren-Herlenius), which is a data-accrual point and not a maturity objection to B046.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann and a postdoctoral link to Paul Greengard; neither is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and he flags them as transparency background, not recusal grounds.
El Manira discloses a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, and use of optogenetics as a field; none of these involves a credited name on the shortlist.
Perlmann discloses collaborations with Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson and co-authorship with committee colleagues; none involves a credited candidate.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen on other work; none involves a shortlisted candidate.

Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius report no specific conflict (Wahren-Herlenius notes co-authors Kuchroo and Sonesson are not credited names); no member records a conflict or recusal on any shortlisted ballot.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee settle, from the evidence supplied, whether Mojsov or Habener has the stronger documented claim to identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide? If it cannot, should the credit be left as Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, or should the allocation change?

Should the B046 citation honour the physiology and active peptide of GLP-1, or the development of the long-acting drugs? If the latter, should Knudsen replace Mojsov, or any other credited name, and on what stated grounds?

Is B046 alone the right prize, or should it be paired with a second distinct achievement (CAR-T B028 is named most often)? Since any pairing would require dropping a B046 name under the three-person cap, which name, and would any member then change their preferred configuration?

If a second achievement is considered, how are the Eshhar omission for B028 and the six-way optogenetics attribution for B038 handled, and is there any member who would prefer one of B028, B038, B029, B007 or B011 over a B046 prize part?
Is the maturity concern for cGAS-STING (B029, no approved therapy yet) shared across members, and does it change its standing relative to other alternatives?
Does any member regard the long-term safety evidence on GLP-1 agonists as bearing on the timing or wording of a B046 citation?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete explicit agreement on B046 with identical laureates and no member preferring a different or a two-part configuration. The remaining disagreement is in attribution and scope, not in scientific merit or maturity: Mojsov's priority, Habener's omission, Knudsen's exclusion, and whether a second achievement should share the prize. Every member flags these as unresolved, and the files contain no explicit support for any specific alternative as a prize part. Round 2 should therefore test whether this convergence holds under those attribution and scope questions.
